n: The Lord condemns His “rebellious children” in Judah who make plans and alliances without consulting Him, piling sin on sin. In Hezekiah’s day, Judah sought Egypt’s help against Assyria.

f.g: Make an alliance — literally “pour out a libation,” sealing a treaty.

n: They go down to Egypt for protection without asking the Lord, trusting Pharaoh’s strength and Egypt’s “shade.”

f.w: have not asked at my mouth

n: But Pharaoh’s protection will bring them shame, and Egypt’s shade will bring disgrace.
Judah’s officials have traveled to Zoan and Hanes, important Egyptian cities, seeking an alliance.
Everyone will be ashamed of a nation that cannot help them — Egypt will be useless, bringing only disgrace.
Isaiah pictures envoys hauling treasures on donkeys and camels through the dangerous Negev desert, home of lions and snakes, to buy help from a nation that cannot help.
Egypt’s help is worthless. That’s why God calls it “Rahab who sits still” — a big name that does nothing.

f.w: Their strength is to sit still
f.g: Better “Rahab who sits still”; Rahab was a poetic name for Egypt as a chaos monster (Psalms 87:4).

n: God tells Isaiah to write this on a tablet and in a scroll as a lasting witness for future generations.
Write that they are a rebellious, lying people who refuse to hear the Lord’s instruction.
They tell the seers, “Stop seeing visions,” and the prophets, “Don’t tell us what’s right; tell us pleasant things — even illusions.”
“Get out of our way! Stop confronting us with the Holy One of Israel!” They want religion without God’s demands.

f.w: cause the Holy One of Israel to cease
f.g: Stop talking to us about God.

n: Because they reject God’s word and rely on oppression and deceit instead…
…their sin will be like a cracked, bulging wall that suddenly collapses all at once.

f.g: A crack in a wall about to give way.

n: It will shatter like a clay pot smashed so thoroughly that no piece is big enough to scoop a coal from a fire or water from a cistern.
God had offered a better way: “In returning and rest you will be saved; in quietness and trust is your strength.” But they refused.

f.w: In returning and rest shall ye be saved
in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength

n: They said, “No, we’ll escape on horses!” — so they will flee. “We’ll ride swift horses!” — so their pursuers will be swifter.
A thousand will flee from one attacker, and from five they will all run, until only a lonely flagpole is left on a hilltop. This reverses God’s promise to the faithful.

f.w: One thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one

n: Yet the Lord is waiting to be gracious to them and rises to show mercy. He is a God of justice; blessed are all who wait for Him.

f.w: the LORD wait, that he may be gracious
blessed are all they that wait for him

n: People of Zion in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. When He hears your cry, He will answer graciously.
Though the Lord gives you the bread of hardship and water of affliction, your Teacher will no longer hide; you will see Him with your own eyes.

f.g: The Hebrew may be singular: “thy Teacher” — God Himself.

n: You will hear a voice behind you saying, “This is the way; walk in it,” whenever you turn right or left. Latter-day Saints often connect this with the guidance of the Holy Ghost.

f.w: This is the way, walk ye in it

n: Then you will treat your silver and gold idols as unclean, throwing them away like a filthy rag: “Get out of here!”
God will send rain for your seed, and the land will produce rich, abundant food. Your livestock will graze in wide pastures.
Even the oxen and donkeys that plow will eat the best seasoned fodder, carefully winnowed — a sign of overflowing abundance.
On every high mountain and hill streams will flow, on the day of great slaughter when the towers of the proud fall.
The moon will shine like the sun, and the sun seven times brighter, when the Lord binds up His people’s wounds and heals them. This anticipates the glory of the Millennium.

f.w: the light of the sun shall be sevenfold
healeth the stroke of their wound

n: Look! The Lord comes from afar, burning with anger, His lips full of wrath and His tongue like consuming fire.
His breath is like a flooding torrent rising to the neck. He will shake the nations in a sieve of destruction and put a bridle in their jaws to lead them astray.

f.w: to the midst of the neck

f.g: A sieve that leaves nothing — sifting to destruction.

n: Meanwhile, God’s people will sing as on a holy festival night, with glad hearts like pilgrims going up with flutes to the Lord’s mountain.
The Lord will make His majestic voice heard and show His mighty arm coming down with fierce anger, consuming fire, cloudburst, storm, and hail.

f.w: the lighting down of his arm
f.g: The descending blow of His arm.

n: At the Lord’s voice Assyria, who struck others with a rod, will be shattered.
Every blow of the Lord’s punishing rod on Assyria will be accompanied by tambourines and harps — Judah celebrating as God fights for them.
Long ago a burning place, Topheth, was prepared — deep and wide, piled with wood — for the king. The Lord’s breath, like a stream of burning sulfur, will set it ablaze.

f.g: A site in the Hinnom Valley near Jerusalem where children were burned to Molech (Jeremiah 7:31); later a symbol of hell.
